title: Alpine: Partial Unlabeled Graph Alignment

problem.claim: Partial unlabeled graph alignment seeks to align nodes of two unequal-order graphs without auxiliary labels or attributes while minimizing a distance function.

gap.claim: Existing approaches using dummy nodes or graph embeddings do not adequately address partial graph alignment; in particular, an optimal equal-order alignment with dummy nodes need not yield an optimal partial alignment.

contributions.claim: Introduces Alpine, an algorithm for partial unlabeled graph alignment that uses only graph adjacency matrices.
Uses a tailored objective function inspired by shape-matching techniques together with a state-of-the-art optimization method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show Alpine consistently surpasses state-of-the-art graph alignment methods in solution quality across all benchmark datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Applications require aligning nodes across two graphs by minimizing a distance function.
The practical setting involves unequal-order graphs without auxiliary labels or attributes, termed partial unlabeled graph alignment.
Prior approaches add dummy nodes or use graph embeddings, but dummy-node equal-order optimality does not guarantee partial-alignment optimality.
The paper proposes Alpine, using adjacency matrices, a tailored shape-matching-inspired objective, and a state-of-the-art optimization method.
The authors report that Alpine outperforms state-of-the-art graph alignment methods in solution quality across all benchmark datasets.

source_observation.claim: The paper reports that converting unequal-order graph alignment into equal-order alignment with dummy nodes can produce a suboptimal partial alignment.

interpretation.claim: A reduction that changes the structure of the optimization problem may not preserve the original problem's optimum.

application.claim: When designing solutions for partial or mismatched data, evaluate whether the transformation preserves the objective and feasible solutions of the original task.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when dummy-node reductions are valid or invalid beyond the reported deficiency.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify Alpine's objective function or optimization procedure.
The abstract does not identify the benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not provide complexity, scalability, ablation, or reproducibility details.
